ideas.title: See the cache hit rate of every worker run, then put Calina's fixed rules first so they can be cached
ideas.problem: Two gaps. (1) control_plane.record_usage() stores cache_tokens as cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens in one number, so nobody can tell a cheap cache read from an expensive cache write, and usage_today() adds them to input and output as 'tokens'. We cannot see whether caching works for our workers at all. (2) The Calina V3 system prompt (agents.py CALINA_SYSTEM_V3, 15,308 characters) puts per-run values at the top: {today} at character 73, {channel} 126, {plan} 186, {count} 214. The prompt is one block and the cache matches an exact prefix, so a change at character 73 (the date) means none of the 14,500 characters of fixed rules after {count} can be reused from an earlier run. Claude Code docs: 'a change to the per-request part changes the whole system prompt, so the static instructions miss the cache too'. Calina runs a batch, up to two rewrites per script, and a topic rewrite, each a new `claude -p` process (workers.run).
ideas.gain: Step 1 gives the missing number. Step 2: about 3,600 tokens of fixed rules (14,500 characters / 4) per Calina run read at $0.10 per MTok (Sonnet 5.5, 0.05x) instead of written at $2.50 per MTok (1.25x of $2): roughly $0.009 per run. At 10-30 Calina/Israa-type runs a day that is $0.09-0.27 of the $6.00/day SUBSCRIPTION_DAILY_VALUE_USD for Calina, about 2-5 percent, and the first answer arrives a little faster. If the approved examples block (quality.examples_block, put before the prompt and already fixed) is long, the saving is bigger, because it would also move into the cached part only if it comes before the boundary, which it does. We will know from the new hit-rate figure for Calina, before and after, on 5+ runs each. This is a small saving, not a big one. The reason to do step 1 now is that it costs almost nothing and it tells us whether any further token work is worth the owner's time.
ideas.test: Step 1: run any one worker in practice mode with HQ_WORKER_ENGINE=claude_code (Vera, 16 s), check the usage row has cache_read and cache_write filled and the sum equals the old cache_tokens; run it twice within an hour and check the second run shows a higher cache_read. Step 2 test cases (use `claude -p` with the real prompt file, compare usage.cache_read_input_tokens): (a) normal: two Calina batch runs with different {count} (3 and 5) within 1 hour: the second run's cache_read is at least 3,000 tokens, before the change it is about 0. (b) edge: same project on the next day (new {today}): fixed rules still read from cache if the first run was less than 1 hour earlier; after 1 hour the cache is cold and both versions pay the write, no loss. (c) failure case: an old Claude Code under v2.1.275: the boundary line must not break the output; run one batch and check the scene files still validate (quality.pre_review passes) and the model does not mention the marker. A pass = no change in script quality checks, cache_read goes up in (a), nothing breaks in (c).
ideas.confidence_why: The cache rules and the boundary line are from Claude Code and API docs (A, several pages agree). The size of the saving is my arithmetic from prompt length and list prices, with no measured run from the owner's PC, and no source says how the plan limit counts cache reads. Weakest link: the saving is probably small.
ideas.risks: Step 2 changes the order of a prompt the owner cares about (Calina's script quality). Models can weigh the start of a prompt more, so the plan and the topic moving to the end could change how closely she follows them: run the 3 test cases and compare one batch by Israa's pass rate before shipping. A prompt rule (rules.py prompt.Calina) that replaces the whole prompt must keep the boundary line, or it just loses the cache gain. The new DB columns are additive. No outside code, no licence issue.
